Fixed in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/83349
This sentence isn't correct.  The redfish spec allows many eventlogs in many different locations in parallel.
Done
Reword to something that points out that breaking out logs per host node is hard, so we chose to not do that.  Arguably log per host node is more correct, but we're making tradeoffs here.
Done
This also isn't correct.  Per Redfish, we would put the event log on each host and log per-host messages to each system.  We're making tradeoffs.
Done
Do we really need a separate option for this, or can we just implicitly enable this when we enable multi-host?

This decision was made based on the discussion we had in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/76319.

Having this as an options would solve the 'no host' case.

Also, the way I read the discussion, you lean towards EventLog under Managers. 

I am not sure, whether this is an opinion all share, or an opinion that is shared by a few, the way this is currently implemented lets everyone decide this for themselves, which I think is fair.
typo?  I'm assuming you meant 443
I am testing with qemu and binding port 4443 localhost to 443 qemu.
I don't see redfish service validator being run?
First sentence after 'Tested:' states redfish validation. Updated the statement, to clarify that validation was done on Systems and Managers tree.
if we keep this option, "dbus" needs to show up somewhere in the name, because there are multiple event logs.

From my understanding we currently distinguish between journal and dbus eventlog. What additional event logs would there be? 

The option handles both, depending on whether `redfish-dbus-log` is enabled or not.
This is "Managers" not BMC
Done
Please combine these three methods into one.

Done. Is this something we want for Managers dbus eventlog and ComputerSystem journal/dbus eventlog too?
And in general, is this a new style that we should follow?
Done
Please follow the naming convention, which involves the word "handle" look at the other code for examples.
Done
Why did this move?  It looks like it replaced requestRoutesSystemsEventLogService?

I had to move it, else the redfish test aswell as the redfish routes test would fail. Based on the stacktrace, adding a node to the trie seemed to have failed. Reordering this fixed the issue.

requestRoutesSystemsEventLogService had to be moved into scope of the if statement for Location == "systems".
it is really <redfish-manager-uri-name> and <redfish-system-uri-name>
Done
At this point, the routes for managers dbus eventlog don't exist yet. https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/83355 does apply the same logic.
I guess I would rather have the !BMCWEB_REDFISH_DBUS_LOG here, oh well.
